Hi Samir  thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Summary of needs (from our conversation)
- Primary workload: near-real-time triage and clinical summarization for inbound patient messages (avg request size ~450 tokens, bursts during 8am-10am ET)
- Latency target: 200400ms p95 for single-request autocomplete/chat flows
- Data controls: PHI in payloads; customer must retain audit logs and KMS-managed keys
- Expected steady-state QPS: 1218 req/s, peak 40 req/s for 3045 minutes/day
- Retention & compliance: 7 years for audit logs; SOC 2 required

Deployment modes we discussed
1) Hosted API  fastest to production, usage-based pricing (per-token) with Redwood-managed keys and SOC 2 compliance; good for POC and early rollouts
2) Dedicated capacity  reserved GPU pool, committed monthly/annual capacity; predictable latency and lower unit cost at scale; recommended if you want isolation without on-prem ops
3) Private (VPC / on-prem)  full network isolation and customer-managed infra; best for regulated environments or where data cannot leave cloud region

Suggested next steps
- Ill cc Marissa (pricing) to model economics for your QPS and burst profile across the three modes (per-token vs reserved capacity).
- Can you confirm: expected monthly token volume (approx avg tokens per request * expected req/month) and whether AcmeHealth procurement prefers commits or pay-as-you-go?
- Please share any internal compliance checklist we should address for Private deployment (e.g., firewall/VPN requirements, on-prem hardware constraints).

Attachments: none in this message  will follow with a pricing deck + SOW draft.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Hi Samir  looping in a short cost model and a pricing deck. I built two scenarios (ballpark):

Scenario A  Hosted (per-token)
- Avg tokens/request: 450 tokens (input+output), requests/month: 18 req/s * 3600 * 24 * 30  46.7M requests/month  ~21B tokens/month
- List per-token: $0.00006 per token  Monthly = 21,000,000,000 * $0.00006 = $1,260,000
- Pros: no infra ops, immediate scale; Cons: variable cost and higher at large scale

Scenario B  Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Example committed cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent workers with autoscale to 12 for bursts. Monthly reserved cost (list) estimated: $120k/month (capacity + infra + support)
- Measured throughput for your workload: ~20 req/s sustained per 8-worker cluster with p95 latency ~220ms; burst to 40 req/s using autoscale/burst credits
- Effective unit cost approximated: ~$0.000015 per token (after amortizing committed cost at expected volume)  Monthly  $315,000
- Pros: predictable spend, lower unit cost, isolation; Cons: commit required, provisioning lead time

Scenario C  Private (VPC/on-prem)
- On-prem pricing varies (CAPEX + annual platform fee). If you supply hardware, Redwood charges platform license + support (example: $60k/year platform + integration + per-node agent fee).
- Lead time: 812 weeks for VPC; 1216+ weeks for on-prem (due to procurement + network + install).

Notes & assumptions
- Token math is high-level; I used avg token counts and a 30-day month.
- Dedicated numbers assume a negotiated discount on list infra. Exact price depends on model family and quantization.
- We can reduce Hosted costs with aggressive caching/prefix KV reuse for chat flows and by using a smaller model for routine summarization and the larger model for high-quality outputs only.
